de_lineis_rectis/people/apollonius.title: Apollonius of Perga
de_lineis_rectis/people/apollonius.description: Author of the Conics, celebrated in Ceva’s Prooemium and applied across Liber Secundus and the Appendix Geometrica.

de_lineis_rectis/people/archimedes.title: Archimedes of Syracuse
de_lineis_rectis/people/archimedes.description: Author of On the Equilibrium of Planes (Equiponderants I.6–7), Quadrature of the Parabola, and On the Sphere and Cylinder; foundational authority for Ceva’s Statica Constructio.

de_lineis_rectis/people/borelli.title: Giovanni Alfonso Borelli
de_lineis_rectis/people/borelli.description: Pisan mathematician and editor of Apollonius Books V–VII (1661), mentor of Donato Rossetti, and cited by Ceva in Liber Secundus, Lemma I.

de_lineis_rectis/people/caravaggio.title: Pietro Paolo Caravaggio Jr.
de_lineis_rectis/people/caravaggio.description: Son of Ceva’s Milanese mentor Pietro Paolo Caravaggio Sr., credited in Liber Primus, Proposition VI (tab. 1. fig. 10) with the pure Euclidean parallel-line proof of cevian concurrency.

de_lineis_rectis/people/carnot.title: Lazare Nicolas Marguerite Carnot
de_lineis_rectis/people/carnot.description: Author of Essai sur la théorie des transversales (1806), reviving and extending Ceva’s and Menelaus’s theorems across polygons and algebraic curves.

de_lineis_rectis/people/cavalieri.title: Bonaventura Cavalieri, O.S.H.
de_lineis_rectis/people/cavalieri.description: Author of Geometria indivisibilibus continuorum (1635); credited in Ceva’s Prooemium with curing his youthful circle-quadrature obstinacy, and critically bounded on curved surfaces at the close of the Appendix…

de_lineis_rectis/people/ceva.title: Giovanni Ceva
de_lineis_rectis/people/ceva.description: Milanese geometer, statician, and court mathematician to Ferdinando Carlo Gonzaga at Mantua; author of De lineis rectis se invicem secantibus statica constructio (Milan, 1678), Opuscula mathematica (1682), Geometria…

de_lineis_rectis/people/clavius.title: Christoph Clavius, S.J.
de_lineis_rectis/people/clavius.description: Jesuit mathematician of the Collegio Romano, cited by Ceva in Liber Primus on compound-ratio manipulation (Euclidis Elementorum Libri XV).

de_lineis_rectis/people/commandino.title: Federico Commandino
de_lineis_rectis/people/commandino.description: Translator of Euclid, Archimedes, Apollonius, Serenus (1566), and Pappus (1588), and author of Liber de centro gravitatis solidorum (1565); cited by Ceva on compound ratios and solid centroids.

de_lineis_rectis/people/euclid.title: Euclid of Alexandria
de_lineis_rectis/people/euclid.description: Author of the Elements (Stoicheia), Books I, V, VI, XI, and XII, supplying the proportional and area-ratio foundations of Caravaggio Jr.’s Prop. VI and Ceva’s Appendix Geometrica.

de_lineis_rectis/people/gergonne.title: Joseph Diez Gergonne
de_lineis_rectis/people/gergonne.description: Projective geometer after whom the incircle-contact concurrency point X(7) (proved in Ceva’s 1678 Liber Secundus, Prop. I) is named.

de_lineis_rectis/people/gonzaga.title: Ferdinando Carlo Gonzaga-Nevers
de_lineis_rectis/people/gonzaga.description: Tenth Duke of Mantua, Montferrat, and Guastalla, patron and dedicatee of Ceva’s 1678 treatise.

de_lineis_rectis/people/hippocrates.title: Hippocrates of Chios
de_lineis_rectis/people/hippocrates.description: Pioneer of curvilinear lune quadrature, re-proved synthetically by Ceva in Appendix Geometrica, Proposition II.

de_lineis_rectis/people/kimberling.title: Clark Kimberling
de_lineis_rectis/people/kimberling.description: Creator of the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers (ETC, geometor/etc), indexing tens of thousands of barycentric and isotomic concurrencies governed by Ceva’s Theorem.

de_lineis_rectis/people/menelaus.title: Menelaus of Alexandria
de_lineis_rectis/people/menelaus.description: Author of the Sphaerica (Book III, Lemma 1), whose collinear transversal theorem Ceva re-proves by two-lever statics in Liber Primus, Elementum I and Proposition VIII.

de_lineis_rectis/people/moebius.title: August Ferdinand Möbius
de_lineis_rectis/people/moebius.description: Author of Der barycentrische Calcul (1827), formalizing Ceva’s positive and negative static weights (F - A) into homogeneous barycentric coordinates.

de_lineis_rectis/people/monza.title: Ludovico Monza
de_lineis_rectis/people/monza.description: Master Milanese printer (Ex Typographia Ludovici Montiae) of the 1678 editio princeps, noted for setting algebraic addition with the obelus/dagger † (A † F).

de_lineis_rectis/people/mutaman.title: Yusuf al-Mu’taman ibn Hud
de_lineis_rectis/people/mutaman.description: Hudid King of Zaragoza whose Arabic Kitāb al-Istikmāl contained the earliest surviving synthetic proof of the cevian concurrency theorem (unknown in Latin Europe and rediscovered by J. P. Hogendijk in 1985).

de_lineis_rectis/people/nagel.title: Christian Heinrich von Nagel
de_lineis_rectis/people/nagel.description: Investigator of the excircle-contact point X(8), isotomic conjugate of X(7) via Ceva’s Liber Secundus, Prop. I Corollarium.

de_lineis_rectis/people/pappus.title: Pappus of Alexandria
de_lineis_rectis/people/pappus.description: Author of the Synagoge (Books VII & VIII), preserving ancient projective harmonic invariance and mechanics.

de_lineis_rectis/people/ptolemy.title: Claudius Ptolemy
de_lineis_rectis/people/ptolemy.description: Author of the Almagest (Book I.13), transmitting the planar and spherical Menelaus sector configuration in compound-ratio form.

de_lineis_rectis/people/rossetti.title: Donato Rossetti
de_lineis_rectis/people/rossetti.description: Canon of Livorno and Professor at the University of Pisa, gratefully honored in Ceva’s 1678 Prooemium as his beloved teacher.

de_lineis_rectis/people/serenus.title: Serenus of Antinoöpolis
de_lineis_rectis/people/serenus.description: Author of On the Section of a Cylinder, cited by Ceva in Liber Secundus, Lemma I to project tangent ratios from circles onto ellipses.

de_lineis_rectis/people/tommaso-ceva.title: Tommaso Ceva, S.J.
de_lineis_rectis/people/tommaso-ceva.description: Younger brother of Giovanni Ceva, celebrated Jesuit mathematician, humanist, and poet; long-serving professor of mathematics at the Jesuit Brera College in Milan, inventor of the mathematical trisection instrument…

de_lineis_rectis/people/torricelli.title: Evangelista Torricelli
de_lineis_rectis/people/torricelli.description: Author of Opera geometrica (1644), cited in Ceva’s Appendix Geometrica on the 2 : 1 paraboloid centroid and the acute infinite hyperbolic solid.

de_lineis_rectis/people/valerio.title: Luca Valerio
de_lineis_rectis/people/valerio.description: Author of De centro gravitatis solidorum libri tres (1604), hailed by Ceva in Appendix Geometrica as “subtilissimus nostri æui Archimedes” for the 5 : 3 hemisphere centroid.
